name: Gordon Ryan Mount Control System
description: Explore Gordon Ryan Mount Control System with a matched BJJ Fanatics course, practical study steps, partner drills, and connected technique references.
summary: The Gordon Ryan Mount Control System is a study framework for maintaining mount through escape reactions before isolating an arm for a submission.
overview:
Reaching mount and keeping mount are different training problems. This guide gives the second problem its own practice structure before adding attacks. Gordon Ryan's mount course provides the technical companion: its syllabus links entries, maintenance, arm isolation and high-mount developments, with rolling analysis for comparison. Use the footage to form questions about your own exchanges; a successful demonstration does not establish that the same control is already reliable in your rounds.

The sequence and drills below are original BJJGraph study suggestions, not a course transcript or an official instructor curriculum. Use the linked demonstrations for technical detail, then compare one selected lesson with a controlled partner round.
key_principles: Begin from a familiar side pin and identify the contact that should survive the transition to mount.
Give the bottom partner a bridge or knee-elbow recovery objective and study what changes before the escape succeeds.
Explore the cross-wrist or underhook route while measuring whether your base remains stable.
Compare staying low with advancing toward high mount or S mount when the arms and hips allow it.
Add one agreed submission entry and record whether the positional control survives the attempt.

Re-establish balance before trying to improve the attacking position.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph practice suggestion: start from Mount and give the partner one agreed response. Work through the first two stages cooperatively, then stop each repetition at the chosen control or recovery endpoint. Add another reaction only when both partners can explain what changed. Keep submission entries controlled and release immediately on a tap or request to stop. Review the lost connection before adding speed.

products.title: Systematically Attacking From Top Pins: Mount
products.blurb: A directly matched instructional companion for maintaining mount through escape reactions before isolating an arm for a submission. Review its published contents and sample to judge the teaching approach.
products.best_for: No-gi top players who reach mount but lose it during bridges, knee-elbow recovery, or early submission attempts.
products.study_focus: Prioritise the mount-maintenance material, then study the cross-wrist and underhook pathways into arm isolation before watching the rolling commentary.
products.practice_tip: BJJGraph suggestion: begin with 'Rehearse the arrival' from Side Control. Record which partner response interrupts the plan and revisit that lesson before adding another branch.
